interpretation: The committed count is strictly monotone across every legitimate act and even across an explicit rollback attempt, which itself only ever raises the count -- confirming no operation restores a prior state. A value cached at an earlier count and returned as a 'fetch' once the graph has since grown is numerically stale relative to a fresh search against the current graph, the direct computational confirmation of Proposition 10.5's fetch-incoherence argument.
theorem: Theorem 10.6 (Monotone History), Remark 10.7 (No Caching Across Sessions)
